page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier status in stress-ng multi-core testing, passmark CPU score, and memory bandwidth for both small and large block read-only operations. It also demonstrates top-tier performance in static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations, alongside strong database operations in PassMark. However, single-threaded performance is more moderate, with average ratings in Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression.

While prompt processing for large language models registers in the top tier or strong categories, text generation speeds for smaller models are relatively weak, highlighting a performance tradeoff in sequential generation tasks without GPU acceleration. Given the high memory density, dedicated CPU allocation, and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and memory-bound enterprise applications.

This profile makes the instance highly suitable for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation.
